goal: - The diagram shows at a fixed zoom, about 3 or 4 boxes tall, in a phone-shaped area
- Clicking an answer scrolls so the next question and its answers are in view
- The Reset button scrolls back to the top
- The current full-picture view is still available with a switch
notInScope: - The real mobile app; task 1 owns it
- Changes to the diagram file
- Touch or swipe gestures
problemSolvedByTask: Both: the whole diagram is too big, and I want to see how the mobile app will feel if we made moving between precision points feel like animated scrolling
description: index.html renders the whole diagram into #diagram inside #output (overflow: auto) with mermaid.render() and no zoom control; the SVG scales to fit. The next question after a click is the last Q_ node in the walkTrail() result. Needed: a phone-shaped viewport (fixed width, fixed height) around the SVG at a fixed scale so 3 or 4 boxes are visible; after each click, find the SVG element for the next question (id contains 'flowchart-<ID>-') and scrollIntoView with smooth behavior so the question and its answer boxes are in view; the Reset button scrolls back to the top; a switch toggles between this phone view and the current full view. Only index.html changes.

title: Interactive node editor in web view that rewrites the .mmd file
userDescription:
An interactive GUI editor mode: you select a node and  can do things like:
- add a question after
- add a block after
- remove a question
- remove a block
- add a choice to a question
- remove a choice to a question. 
- double-click a block to change the text
The editor should be smart about how it handles nodes being removed/inserted into the graph.
The changes made to the graph are written into the .mmd file.
goal: - In web view (phone view off), clicking a node selects it and shows actions: add question after, add block after, remove question, remove block, add choice, remove choice; double-click on a node opens inline text editing.
- Removing a question shows a preview of each candidate replacement path (one per choice) that the user can cycle through, with a cancel button; confirming reconnects the parent to the chosen path.
- Removing a choice removes only that choice node; everything reachable from it stays in the file as an orphaned path.
- After every action the diagrams/<name>.mmd file on disk contains the change, and reloading the page shows the same drawing.
- After every action the saved .mmd parses with mermaid with no syntax error.
- Undo and redo of editor actions work, and each undo/redo is written to the .mmd file.
- The e2e tests in the tests field pass on diagrams/say-something-or-let-it-go.mmd, and the existing 11 tests in tests/index.html.test.ts still pass.
notInScope: - Editing in phone view; phone view stays read-only (no owning task yet).
- Drag to move or re-link nodes (no owning task yet).
- Cleaning up orphaned paths left by removing a choice (no owning task yet).
problemSolvedByTask: Editing diagrams by hand is slow and error-prone
description: This task builds a functional, not pretty, MVP of a mermaidflow.app-style visual editor for this project's diagrams; editor mode is always on in web view (phone view off), with no new toggle. viewer.ts only renders mermaid source from the codeBox textarea and handles answer-node clicks (outputBox click listener, nodeIdOf, isAnswerId, choicesOf, parentOf); nothing mutates graph structure yet. Diagram files under diagrams/*.mmd use flowchart TD: a "question" is a decision diamond, ID{"label"}, with choice nodes ID_Y/ID_N/ID_ONCE/ID_NONE/ID_MULTIPLE, and a "block" is a static rectangle, ID["label"] or ID[label]; edges are A --> B, parsed by parseEdges -- mermaidflow.app has no separate term for a branch/condition node, so these project terms stay. mermaidflow.app's "add nodes and edges" maps to this task's "add node after": inserting a question or block after a selected node splices into the edge chain. mermaidflow.app has no documented term for "delete node"; here it means removing a question (with a cycling preview of each choice's replacement path plus a cancel button) or removing a block, always reconnecting predecessors to successors, while removing a choice only orphans its subtree without deleting it. mermaidflow.app's "Label: Edit text content" maps to this task's "edit label": double-click on a question or block opens inline text editing. mermaidflow.app's "Undo and Redo buttons" map directly to this task's undo/redo requirement: every editor action, and its undo/redo, is written to the .mmd file. Saving exists end to end via saveBtn PUTing codeBox.value to /api/diagrams/:name, which server.js writes to diagrams/<name>.mmd; the editor should rewrite codeBox.value (node lines, edge lines, class lines) and reuse that path so mermaidflow.app's "Text Tab and visual editor work together in real-time" -- code and diagram stay in sync -- and reloading the page shows the same drawing. Tests drive the app over the Chrome DevTools Protocol against server.js on port 3000 (tests/index.html.test.ts); no existing test exercises node or edge mutation.
tests: Using 'say-something-or-let-it-go.mmd' as the test base, a test that adds a new question at the end with 2 choices, a test that inserts a question in the middle of the graph with 2 choices, a test that inserts static blocks at the end, a test that inserts static blocks in the middle, a test that removes a choice, and test that adds a new choice to an existing question, a test that modifies the text of a question, a test that modifies the text of a static block.  Each test should also verify that the syntax of the resulting .mmd diagram is 100% valid, in addition to what the test is already verifying.

title: Floating node inspectors with explicit destination selection
userDescription: Follow plans/task-22-node-inspector-and-destinations.md as the decision-complete implementation specification. Replace task 21's shared action bar with the three floating node inspectors in the supplied mockup and add an explicit Destination workflow so graph editing never has to guess where a new or existing path should lead. Every inspector has a bordered Text field plus Undo, Redo, and Cancel/Close. Decision block: [Remove][Remove choices] / [add choice] / [insert static block before] / [insert Decision & leading choice before] / [Undo][Redo] / [Cancel]. static block: [Remove] / [insert static block before] / [add Decision block after] / [insert Decision & leading choice before] / [Undo][Redo] / [Cancel or Close] / [Destination]. choice block: [Remove] / [add Decision block after] / [add static block after] / [Undo][Redo] / [Cancel or Close] / [Destination]. Destination is always present for static and choice blocks and offers, in order: Terminal, New static block, New Decision block, then every viable existing static or Decision block. It shows the current connection and lets the user terminate, create, or rewire a path. Every committed text, graph, undo, or redo change is validated and persisted to the current .mmd file.
chainGoal: - Tasks 21 and 22 together deliver a usable GUI editor for .mmd diagrams in web view: task 21 supplies graph rewriting, persistence, and history; task 22 provides the floating inspectors and explicit destination selection needed to build, terminate, splice, and reconnect paths without hand-editing Mermaid text.
goal: - In web view, clicking a node opens one rounded floating inspector beside its SVG node, over the drawing and clamped inside the visible diagram area. Selecting, retargeting, dismissing, or rerendering the inspector preserves both scrollLeft and scrollTop of the diagram container.

- The inspector's normal state matches the mockup: a centered title exactly identifying `Decision block`, `static block`, or `choice block`; one `Text:` row with an obvious bordered input containing the current label; a two-column control grid in the exact row order from userDescription; Undo and Redo share a row; and Cancel/Close spans both columns. Controls not listed for that node kind are absent, not merely disabled.

- Decision block exposes Remove, Remove choices, add choice, insert static block before, and insert Decision & leading choice before. static block exposes Remove, insert static block before, add Decision block after, and insert Decision & leading choice before. choice block exposes Remove, add Decision block after, and add static block after.

- The Text input edits Decision, static, and choice labels. Enter validates and writes the input value into the selected node in the loaded .mmd file; double-clicking a node opens its inspector and focuses/selects the input. Cancel/Close, Escape, or clicking empty drawing space discards uncommitted input and closes the inspector; clicking another node discards uncommitted input, moves the inspector, and retargets every action.

- Every static and choice inspector shows a `Destination:` select below Cancel/Close, even when already connected. Its options are exactly Terminal, New static block, New Decision block, then every existing static and Decision node in .mmd source order. Existing-node options always display `label (node ID)`, exclude the selected node, and are deduplicated by ID. Descendants remain eligible so intentional cycles are allowed without warning. Decisions never show Destination because they connect through choices.

- A static or choice has at most one outgoing edge. Destination selects its current target or Terminal; selecting the current value is a no-op. Choosing another existing target replaces the sole outgoing edge. Choosing Terminal removes it. In both cases the former target and its downstream path remain in the source as an orphaned branch.

- Choosing New static block, from either Destination or an add-after button, immediately replaces the selected block's outgoing edge with `selected --> NewStatic`; NewStatic is terminal, the former destination remains orphaned, and the inspector moves to NewStatic with Text focused. This does not automatically splice NewStatic into the former path.

- Choosing New Decision block, from either entry point, immediately replaces the outgoing edge with `selected --> NewDecision --> NewChoice`, where NewDecision has exactly one explicit terminal choice. The former destination remains orphaned. Focus NewDecision's Text first; Enter commits it and advances to NewChoice with Destination focused. `add choice` likewise creates one terminal explicit choice, moves to it, and focuses Destination.

- Add-after buttons and their Destination-menu equivalents use the same implementation and produce identical source, selection, focus, save, and history behavior. Each structural or Destination change is one immediate undoable save. If Text is dirty when Destination changes, commit Text first and Destination second as two ordered undo entries.

- A terminal static or choice labels the dismissal button Close; connected static/choice blocks and Decisions label it Cancel. Dismissal never reverses a committed creation or connection; Undo does. Before-insertion actions continue to splice incoming edges automatically and do not open Destination.

- `insert static block before` redirects every incoming edge through one new static block and then to the selected node; with no predecessor the new block becomes a root leading to the selected node. `insert Decision & leading choice before` similarly creates one new Decision and one explicit leading choice between that Decision and the selected node, preserving the rule that a Decision points directly only to choices.

- Keep task 21's Remove behaviors: Decision Remove uses the replacement-path preview/cycle/confirm flow; static Remove reconnects every predecessor to every successor; choice Remove removes the choice and its incident edges while leaving its downstream path orphaned. Remove choices removes every outgoing Decision branch representation-independently: delete labelled outgoing branch edges, and delete immediate explicit choice nodes plus their incident edges, while retaining downstream nodes and paths as orphans. The temporary Decision-removal preview may replace the normal controls and retains its confirm/cycle/cancel controls.

- Inspector Undo/Redo and two always-visible web-header Undo/Redo buttons share task 21's source history and accurately reflect availability. Every commit truncates the redo tail; every action, undo, and redo validates with Mermaid before updating the textarea, rerendering, and saving diagrams/<name>.mmd. Reloading reproduces the same graph.

- A committed text or before-insertion action keeps the original node selected and reanchors its inspector after rerender; add-after and add-choice actions retarget it as described above; removing the selected node closes it. Undo/Redo keeps and reanchors the selection when that node still exists, otherwise it closes the inspector.

- Rewrites preserve valid existing Mermaid source forms used by the project, including standalone and inline node declarations, chained edges, labelled branches, dotted edges, class directives, fan-in, and fan-out; generated IDs are unique and edited labels are safely escaped. The existing suite and the task 22 end-to-end coverage pass.
notInScope: - Editing in phone view; phone view stays read-only (no owning task yet).
- Dragging nodes, manually drawing/relinking edges, or changing layout direction.

problemSolvedByTask: Destination dropdown lies about the graph
description: Confirmed root cause in viewer.ts: renderNodeInspector's destination-options loop (~line 1114-1117) skips any candidate node with kind === 'choice', so outgoingDestination(node.id, graph) can return an id that was never added as an <option>, leaving destinationSelect.value unmatched and silently defaulting to the 'Terminal' option (value ''). Node kind is assigned in the graph parser (viewer.ts ~line 570-574) by a naming-convention heuristic (id starts with fromId + '_' plus an unlabeled edge), not a reliable structural signal, so a real destination node can still be misclassified as 'choice'. Fix is to stop excluding kind === 'choice' candidates from the options loop (or otherwise guarantee the true destination always has a matching option) so destinationSelect.value correctly reflects outgoingDestination(node.id, graph).
tests: Load a diagram with a static/choice node that already has a real outgoing edge to an existing block, select that node, and assert destinationSelect.value equals the real destination's id (not '' / Terminal).
